Navigates core -> page2, goes back, then forward again, and reads the second document's heading. [scenario:nav_forward_after_back driver:ferrum]
Sets location.hash in-page and confirms both the hash and that no document reload happened (a marker global survives). [scenario:nav_hash_change driver:ferrum]
Pushes a same-document history entry with a query string and derives the new search plus proof that the document did not reload. [scenario:nav_push_state driver:ferrum]
Pushes a same-document entry, then drives history back through the driver and confirms the original URL is restored without a reload. [scenario:nav_push_state_back driver:ferrum]
Navigates to an endpoint that 302-redirects twice before landing on a page carrying a redirect-count marker. The driver must settle on the FINAL document. [scenario:nav_redirect_chain driver:ferrum]

Fills an input, reloads the page, and confirms the fresh document no longer carries the typed value. Exercises Page.reload semantics: a real reload must produce a new document, not restore transient DOM state. [scenario:nav_reload_resets_dom driver:ferrum]

Navigates to the core fixture, reloads it, and re-reads #title. Exercises the reload lifecycle: the driver must drive a fresh document load and still resolve the selector against the reloaded page. [scenario:nav_reload_title driver:ferrum]

Answers with the live document title joined with the pathname — the most basic observation pair every driver must expose. [scenario:obs_title_url_surface driver:ferrum]
Computes a visibility matrix over a visible and a hidden element from live layout state. [scenario:obs_visibility_matrix driver:ferrum]
Sets a cookie via document.cookie and parses it back out of the cookie string. [scenario:st_cookie_document_roundtrip driver:ferrum]

Writes two keys, removes one, and derives which keys remain. [scenario:st_storage_remove driver:ferrum]

An element visible at load is display:none'd after 300ms. Waits for the hidden state via a predicate and reports it; a driver that only waits for presence passes too early. [scenario:wait_element_hidden driver:ferrum]

Logs in, types a filter prefix, and answers with the live match counter. [scenario:app_filter_narrows driver:selenium]
Logs in, filters to the gizmo group, adds the first match, and answers with its cart line. [scenario:app_filter_then_add driver:selenium]
Runs the entire flow and answers with greeting plus receipt, every part server-computed. [scenario:app_full_flow_aggregate driver:selenium]
Clears any leftover session cookie, reloads, and confirms the server refuses the item list. [scenario:app_locked_without_login driver:selenium]
Fills the user field, logs in, and answers with the greeting the server echoed back. [scenario:app_login_greets driver:selenium]
Logs in, logs out, and answers with the server farewell plus the relocked list marker. [scenario:app_logout_locks driver:selenium]
Logs in, adds one item twice, and answers with the cart line plus total. [scenario:app_qty_accumulates driver:selenium]
Logs in, adds two items, removes one, and answers with the corrected total. [scenario:app_remove_item driver:selenium]

Sets a window global in one evaluate call and derives a value from it in a second call. A driver that evaluates each expression in a throwaway context (or a fresh isolated world) fails here. [scenario:cs_eval_context_persists driver:selenium]

Sets a window global on the first page, then creates a new page on the same URL and confirms the global is absent. Exercises that new targets get fresh execution contexts rather than reusing the old page's world. [scenario:cs_fresh_page_no_stale_globals driver:selenium]

Navigates and immediately asks the page for its readyState through the driver's evaluate surface. A driver that returns from goto before the document settles fails here. [scenario:cs_ready_state_complete driver:selenium]

Navigates the first page to the core fixture, creates a second page, navigates it to /page2 and reads its heading. The first page's location must not constrain the second target's navigation. [scenario:cs_second_page_independent_nav driver:selenium]

Creates three pages in sequence, navigating each, and reads the heading from the last one. Exercises session/bookkeeping stability across repeated target creation within one attempt. [scenario:cs_session_survives_three_pages driver:selenium]

Fills an input on the first page, then creates a second page on the same fixture and confirms its input is untouched. Exercises multi-target isolation within one driver session. [scenario:cs_two_pages_isolated driver:selenium]

Reads the user agent through the driver's own identity surface and through page JavaScript. Exercises the session's identity plumbing end to end; every engine spoofs a Mozilla-family UA, so the page-observed value must contain 'Mozilla/'. [scenario:cs_ua_surface driver:selenium]

Navigates to the core fixture and reads the current URL through the driver's own url surface (not page JS). The reported location must contain the fixture path. [scenario:cs_url_surface driver:selenium]

Clicks #counter-btn three times on the probe controls page; each click increments the #press-count output via a JS handler. Reads the final tally. Exercises repeated pointer dispatch and observation of client-side state accumulation. [scenario:dyn_counter_clicks driver:selenium]

On the paging fixture each #next click advances a counter and fetches that page's datum over XHR. The final datum P3-FINAL-73 exists only on page 3, reachable after two clicks, so it can only be read by waiting for each async update. Exercises polling/event-driven waiting across real network round-trips. [scenario:dyn_paging_final driver:selenium]

Checks the #checkbox input and reads its live .checked property via evaluate. Exercises the check contract: the driver must toggle the control to a checked state observable on the DOM property, not merely dispatch a click. [scenario:form_checkbox_check driver:selenium]

Checks the #agree checkbox on the probe controls page; the change handler writes 'checked' into #agree-out. Reads it back. Unlike a bare .checked read, this asserts the driver's check dispatches a real change event the page can react to. [scenario:form_checkbox_event driver:selenium]
Fills the same input twice; fill semantics require clear-then-set, so only the second value must remain. [scenario:form_fill_overwrites driver:selenium]

Fills the #field text input with a distinctive value and reads it back via input_value. Exercises the fill contract end to end: the driver must set the input's live value and observe it, proving keyboard/value semantics rather than just a DOM attribute. [scenario:form_fill_readback driver:selenium]
Focuses the core text field through each driver's public route or documented Runtime.evaluate fallback, then verifies the page's active element. [scenario:form_focus_active_element driver:selenium]
Clicks the label (not the checkbox) and reads the change-handler output; label activation semantics must reach the associated control. [scenario:form_label_click_toggles driver:selenium]
Presses Enter inside a text field whose keydown handler records the event; exercises real key-event dispatch, not value mutation. [scenario:form_press_enter_handler driver:selenium]
Clicks the second radio in a group and derives which one the group reports as checked. [scenario:form_radio_pick driver:selenium]

Selects the Engineering option in the #dept dropdown on the probe controls page; the page's change handler writes 'picked:eng' into #dept-out. Reads it back. Exercises select_option and confirms the driver triggers the change event rather than only setting value. [scenario:form_select_option driver:selenium]

Fills the query input, clicks submit, waits for the reloaded document, and reads the server-echoed query value. Exercises the full fill -> submit -> navigation -> readback chain. [scenario:form_submit_roundtrip driver:selenium]
Fills a textarea and reads its live value through the driver. [scenario:form_textarea_fill driver:selenium]

Both static children post a greeting on load; the parent collects them and answers with the sorted join, proving frame scripts executed and the message channel works. [scenario:fr_child_posts_parent driver:selenium]

Sets a marker on the parent, navigates the first child frame to a new URL, and answers with the child's new message plus proof the parent was not reloaded. [scenario:fr_child_self_navigation driver:selenium]

Inserts an iframe served from the localhost alias of the fixture origin (different origin string, same server), waits for it to load, and confirms the same-origin policy throws SecurityError on document access. [scenario:fr_cross_origin_blocked driver:selenium]
Inserts a third iframe after load and reads its script-computed message once the new frame's document is live. [scenario:fr_dynamic_iframe_attach driver:selenium]
Counts frames before and after inserting a child that itself embeds a grandchild, answering with the observed growth of the reachable same-origin tree. [scenario:fr_frame_tree_shape driver:selenium]
Records the initial frame count, removes the first static iframe, waits for the tree to shrink, and answers with the before:after counts. [scenario:fr_iframe_detach driver:selenium]

Inserts a child that embeds its own child; the top document reads the grandchild's script-computed message through two levels of same-origin frame traversal. [scenario:fr_nested_two_levels driver:selenium]
Pokes a computed value into child A's note element and answers with both children's notes, proving sibling frame documents are distinct. [scenario:fr_sibling_isolation driver:selenium]
Waits for both static children to load and reads the first child's script-computed message through the frame tree. [scenario:fr_static_child_read driver:selenium]
Reads #lead + .next through the driver's text surface. [scenario:loc_adjacent_sibling driver:selenium]

Clicks a button addressed by [data-x="go-7"] and reads its handler output. Exercises attribute-selector support in the driver's element resolution. [scenario:loc_attribute_selector_click driver:selenium]
Counts .card elements through the driver's count surface. [scenario:loc_class_count driver:selenium]
Reads #zone .value where an identical .value also exists outside #zone; the scoped match must win. [scenario:loc_descendant_scope driver:selenium]
Clicks .btn where two buttons match; querySelector semantics require the FIRST one, whose handler records its rank. [scenario:loc_first_match_semantics driver:selenium]
Waits for a srcdoc iframe's document and reads a value computed inside it via contentDocument traversal. [scenario:loc_iframe_same_origin_read driver:selenium]
Both the top document and the iframe contain #dup. The driver's selector surface must return the TOP document's element. [scenario:loc_iframe_scope_top_document driver:selenium]
Reads a selector that matches nothing; the op must fail cleanly (step_fails) and the attempt derives its answer from that failure. [scenario:loc_missing_element_fails_cleanly driver:selenium]
Reads li:nth-child(2) from a three-item list through the driver's text surface. [scenario:loc_nth_child_text driver:selenium]
The page attaches a closed shadow root; element.shadowRoot must be null while the host still renders. Confirms closed-mode encapsulation. [scenario:loc_shadow_closed_hidden driver:selenium]

The page attaches an open shadow root at load. Reads the shadow content via explicit shadowRoot traversal - the engine must implement attachShadow and expose shadowRoot. [scenario:loc_shadow_open_pierce driver:selenium]

Fills #textbox with a five-character value on the probe controls page; the input handler writes the live length into #textbox-len. Reads it back. Exercises selector resolution plus input-event-derived DOM observation. [scenario:locator_textbox_len driver:selenium]
Opens two live targets, reads a distinct heading from each, and aggregates both values in the second tab through same-origin session state. [scenario:multi_tab_collect driver:selenium]
Navigates core -> page2, then drives the browser's history back through the driver's own surface and confirms the first document's heading is restored. [scenario:nav_back_restores driver:selenium]

Navigates to the core fixture, then to a second page, and reads the second page's #title. Exercises a second full navigation (document swap) and confirms the driver observes the new document rather than the stale first one. [scenario:nav_cross_page driver:selenium]
Navigates core -> page2, goes back, then forward again, and reads the second document's heading. [scenario:nav_forward_after_back driver:selenium]
Sets location.hash in-page and confirms both the hash and that no document reload happened (a marker global survives). [scenario:nav_hash_change driver:selenium]
Pushes a same-document history entry with a query string and derives the new search plus proof that the document did not reload. [scenario:nav_push_state driver:selenium]
Pushes a same-document entry, then drives history back through the driver and confirms the original URL is restored without a reload. [scenario:nav_push_state_back driver:selenium]

Navigates to an endpoint that 302-redirects twice before landing on a page carrying a redirect-count marker. The driver must settle on the FINAL document. [scenario:nav_redirect_chain driver:selenium]

Fills an input, reloads the page, and confirms the fresh document no longer carries the typed value. Exercises Page.reload semantics: a real reload must produce a new document, not restore transient DOM state. [scenario:nav_reload_resets_dom driver:selenium]

Navigates to the core fixture, reloads it, and re-reads #title. Exercises the reload lifecycle: the driver must drive a fresh document load and still resolve the selector against the reloaded page. [scenario:nav_reload_title driver:selenium]

Pushes one history entry, replaces it in place, then navigates back once. If replaceState correctly rewrote the pushed entry, a single back lands on the original URL with no query string. A driver or engine that materialises replaceState as an extra entry lands on the intermediate URL instead. [scenario:nav_replace_state_collapses_entry driver:selenium]

Navigates to an endpoint that holds the response for 1.2s before serving the document. A driver that gives up early or reads before the body arrives fails. [scenario:nav_slow_document driver:selenium]

Opens a page, navigates to the core fixture, and reads the #title heading text. Exercises the most basic navigation + DOM-read contract that every driver must honor. [scenario:nav_title_read driver:selenium]
Control case for the family: with no interception armed, the page fetch must hit the real endpoint and compute from the server payload. [scenario:net_route_passthrough driver:selenium]
Reads the bounding box of a 120x48 element and answers with its rounded dimensions — the box-model observation surface. [scenario:obs_box_model_geometry driver:selenium]
Answers with the live document title joined with the pathname — the most basic observation pair every driver must expose. [scenario:obs_title_url_surface driver:selenium]
Computes a visibility matrix over a visible and a hidden element from live layout state. [scenario:obs_visibility_matrix driver:selenium]
Sets a cookie via document.cookie and parses it back out of the cookie string. [scenario:st_cookie_document_roundtrip driver:selenium]
Sets a cookie, reloads, and parses the cookie back. Exercises cookie-jar persistence across navigation. [scenario:st_cookie_survives_reload driver:selenium]
Writes a localStorage key and reads it back through a second evaluate call. The value is computed at write time, never present in the page. [scenario:st_local_roundtrip driver:selenium]

Writes localStorage in the first page, creates a second page on the same origin, and reads the key there. Same-origin pages must observe one storage area. [scenario:st_local_shared_same_origin driver:selenium]
Writes a localStorage key, reloads the page, and reads the key back. Exercises storage persistence across the driver's reload path. [scenario:st_local_survives_reload driver:selenium]

Writes sessionStorage in the first page, creates a fresh page on the same origin, and confirms the key is absent there - sessionStorage is per top-level browsing context. [scenario:st_session_isolated_new_page driver:selenium]
Writes and reads a sessionStorage key within one page session. [scenario:st_session_storage_roundtrip driver:selenium]
Writes two keys, removes one, and derives which keys remain. [scenario:st_storage_remove driver:selenium]
An attribute is set 300ms after load. Waits for it via predicate, then reads it through the driver's attribute surface (not page JS). [scenario:wait_attribute_set driver:selenium]

An element visible at load is display:none'd after 300ms. Waits for the hidden state via a predicate and reports it; a driver that only waits for presence passes too early. [scenario:wait_element_hidden driver:selenium]

A button starts disabled and is enabled 350ms after load; its click handler is attached at enable time. Waits for enablement, clicks, and reads the handler's output. [scenario:wait_enabled_then_click driver:selenium]

Navigates to the probe controls page and waits for #late-item, which the page appends via setTimeout ~300ms after load, then reads its text. Exercises event-driven waiting for a DOM node that does not exist at load time. [scenario:wait_late_item driver:selenium]
Three list items are appended at 150/300/450ms. Waits until all three exist and derives the joined item text. [scenario:wait_list_progressive_fill driver:selenium]
Waits for a span inserted 400ms after load and reads its computed text. A driver that only samples the initial DOM misses it. [scenario:wait_slow_badge driver:selenium]
A container holds a spinner that is replaced with content 500ms after load. Waits for the spinner to disappear and reads the replacement. [scenario:wait_spinner_replaced driver:selenium]

The status text changes twice (warming -> phase:1 -> phase:2:W7). Waits for the FINAL state; a driver that returns on the first mutation reads the intermediate value. [scenario:wait_two_phase_settle driver:selenium]

resolved_tasks.description: End-to-end multi-step flow with real Puppeteer: on the paged shop fixture, add gamma on page 1, click next, add keyboard on page 2, click next, add lamp on page 3, then read #cart-total. All clicks ride the real pointer path (on_framework_main_path) and the page re-renders its catalog on every page turn, so stale element handling matters. The expected total '17.40' emerges from cents accumulation (450+990+300)/100 and exists nowhere as a literal in the fixture.
